Publication of an application pursuant to Article 50(2)(a)

SINGLE DOCUMENT

‘Hill Cider’

1.

Name:

‘Hill Cider’

2.

Member State or Third Country:

Exampleland

3.

Description of the agricultural product or foodstuff:

‘Hill Cider’ is a still or lightly sparkling drink obtained by fermenting the juice of apples grown on standard trees.

1. Pressing takes place within a day of picking.

2. No sugar is added.

4.

Concise definition of the geographical area:

The Federal State of Hillshire.

5.

Link with the geographical area:

Cider has been pressed in the hill orchards since the sixteenth century; the cool nights keep the acidity of the fruit high.

The orchards lie between 300 and 600 metres on slopes that face south.

The loam over limestone drains well and the trees root deep.

Pressing houses in the villages have kept the same varieties for generations.

The drink is poured from a stoneware jug into ribbed glasses.

Its reputation is recorded in the market rolls of 1754.
